html:
The National Water Carrier is a system of pipes, canals and tunnels in Israel, finished in 1964, that carries water from the Sea of Galilee in the north to the crowded centre and the dry Negev desert in the south.

Rain falls mainly in the north of the country, while much of the farmland and later the cities lay to the south. Planning began soon after the founding of the state, and the project was the largest Israel had attempted. Water is pumped up from the lake, below sea level, and then flows south by gravity.

Its use of the Jordan basin angered neighbouring Arab states. In 1964 the Arab League planned to divert the Jordan's headwaters in Syria and Lebanon, and Israeli strikes on the works were one of the tensions before the Six-Day War of 1967.

The carrier made farming possible in the Negev, as at the kibbutzim. Since the 2000s, sea-water desalination has supplied most of Israel's drinking water, and the carrier now sometimes pumps water back into the lake.
sum: The National Water Carrier is a system of pipes, canals and tunnels in Israel, finished in 1964, that carries water from the Sea of Galilee in the north to the crowded centre and the dry Negev desert in the south.
